title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Construction of "Case Filing and Petition Reception Windows" in People's Courts (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Circular on Issuing the Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Construction of the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows" of People's Courts (For Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2009] No. 60

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Strengthening the Construction of the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows" of People's Courts are hereby issued to you for your conscientious implementation in light of local conditions.

December 25, 2009

Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Construction of the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows" of People's Courts (For Trial Implementation)

The "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows" of people's courts are important venues for the public to express their demands, participate in litigation, and resolve disputes, and also serve as bridges and bonds for people's courts to understand social conditions and public opinion, serve the litigants involved, and connect with all sectors of society. Over the years, people's courts at all levels have attached importance to strengthening the construction of case-filing and petition reception premises and implementing measures for judicial service to the people, achieving good results. To further implement the guiding ideology of "Three Supremes" for people's court work and establish a good judicial image of people's courts as fair, efficient, close to the people, and convenient for the people, the following opinions are hereby put forward on further strengthening the construction of the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows" of people's courts:

I. General Requirements

1. Adhere to the guiding ideology of "Supremacy of the Party's Cause, Supremacy of the People's Interests, and Supremacy of the Constitution and Laws," focus on the work theme of "Serving the Overall Situation, Administering Justice for the People," combine with the thematic practice activity of "People's Judges for the People," deeply and persistently carry out the construction activity of the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows," build a first-class team, create first-class services, strive for first-class performance, and make it a highlight of the overall work of people's courts.

2. Focus on aspects such as service management, functional layout, facility support, and rules and regulations, correct thinking, improve work style, enhance efficiency, perfect mechanisms, and strengthen the standardization and normalization of the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows," making them judicial service venues with "complete functions, sound systems, complete facilities, and satisfactory services."

II. Basic Functions

1. Litigation Guidance. Designate personnel to be responsible for guiding visitors upon arrival and, according to the purposes and requirements of the visiting public, direct them to the relevant areas.

2. Case-Filing Review. Promptly receive and review case materials, handle case-filing procedures, calculate and collect litigation fees.

3. Case-Filing Mediation. Establish mediation rooms, where judges with rich experience and high professional competence, or full-time people's mediators, retired judges, etc., conduct pre-litigation mediation or case-filing mediation.

4. Relief Services. Provide necessary judicial assistance to parties in financial difficulties, especially those involving elderly, weak, sick, disabled, laid-off workers, migrant workers, etc., seeking alimony, child support, pensions, survivors' benefits, and overdue wages, and decide on the reduction, postponement, or exemption of litigation costs.

5. Inquiry and Consultation. Through counter reception, registration books, touch screens, telephones, the internet, and other means and forms, provide parties with case information inquiry services such as the presiding judge and trial division, trial dates, case progress, enforcement progress, etc. Provide legal consultation services to the visiting public.

6. Material Receipt and Transfer. Receive litigation materials submitted by parties and be responsible for forwarding them to the presiding judge or collegial panel.

7. Post-Judgment Explanation. For questions raised by parties regarding effective judgments, notify the original presiding judge or relevant trial division to provide explanations and clarification, prompting the parties to accept the judgment and refrain from further appeals.

8. Petition Reception. Receive initial visits, appeals, or applications for retrial from the public, divert and guide higher-level or repeated petitions, properly handle collective petitions and other key petitions, maintain orderly petition order in accordance with the law, and ensure the safety of the organ and social stability.

III. Basic Facilities

1. The area of case-filing and petition reception premises shall be constructed in accordance with the "Standards for the Construction of People's Court Courtrooms" (Fa [2002] No. 260, Ministry of Construction Jianbiao [2002] No. 229) and meet the actual needs of the work.

2. Case-filing premises and petition reception premises shall be appropriately separated, with a reasonable layout, dignified and generous appearance, spacious and bright, clean and hygienic.

3. Case-filing and petition reception premises shall be located in places with clear signs, convenient transportation, and easy access for the public.

4. On the premise of ensuring safety and order, the case-filing and petition reception work shall adopt open office modes such as "counter style" or "window style."

5. People's courts shall set up resting seats, drinking water facilities, and sanitary service facilities in the case-filing and petition reception premises, and provide related services such as pens and paper, photocopying, typing, telephones, fax, internet, etc.

6. People's courts shall provide parties with litigation guidance materials such as litigation guides, visitor instructions, and risk disclosure letters. Courts with conditions should equip public screens, electronic touch screens, paging systems, etc.

7. People's courts shall publicly display service commitments, work procedures, management systems, and relevant information about the court and judges in prominent positions.

8. Case-filing and petition reception premises shall be equipped with security inspection equipment such as handheld metal detectors, liquid detectors, channel-type X-ray baggage inspection machines, explosion-proof barrels, and fireproof blankets.

IV. Work Systems

1. First Inquiry Responsibility System. The first staff member to receive a visitor shall conscientiously and responsibly handle the reception. Matters within the scope of duty shall be handled promptly; matters outside the scope of duty shall be promptly transferred to the relevant department and personnel, and the visitor shall be informed of the situation.

2. Service Commitment System. Publicly commit to the processing time, period, and requirements for matters such as case-filing acceptance, petition handling, information inquiry, case consultation, and material transfer, and consciously accept supervision from the public and all sectors of society.

3. Transparency System. Publicly disclose the work responsibilities, work procedures, and other relevant information of case-filing and petition reception; publicly disclose complaint telephone numbers, set up suggestion boxes, designate personnel to handle public complaints, and humbly listen to opinions and suggestions from all sides.

4. Civilized Reception System. Staff shall wear uniforms while on duty, be energetic, dignified in appearance, neatly dressed, well-mannered, provide considerate service, use civilized language (refer to the attached civilized expressions and prohibited expressions), be efficient and timely, and use appropriate methods.

5. Post Responsibility System. Implement fixed posts, fixed personnel, and fixed responsibilities, ensuring clear functions, clear tasks, combination of rights and responsibilities, and evidence-based assessment.

V. Post Requirements

1. Guidance personnel shall use civilized and standardized language to inquire about the purpose of visitors' visits, introduce procedures according to different requirements, guide them to the appropriate locations, and issue service numbers.

2. Case-filing personnel shall carefully review the complaint or appeal materials submitted by the parties, inquire whether they agree to pre-litigation mediation or case-filing mediation. For matters not suitable for mediation, inform them of litigation risks and promptly handle case-filing procedures. Accurately calculate litigation costs and serve relevant litigation documents to the parties. For incomplete materials, guide the parties to complete them at one time; for matters that cannot be filed immediately due to reasons, explain the reasons and agree on a filing date; for matters not within the acceptance scope of people's courts or not under the jurisdiction of this court, provide legal explanations and inform them of the competent unit or agency.

3. Inquiry, consultation, and explanation personnel shall carefully listen to the questions of visitors, patiently answer questions, explain litigation procedures and legal provisions in detail, and provide litigation guidance.

4. Material receipt and transfer personnel shall carefully check and promptly register the litigation materials received; after receiving the materials, notify the relevant trial division to collect them and complete the transfer and handover procedures.

5. Petition reception personnel shall be prompt in reception, patient and meticulous, receive every initial visit, and handle every complaint. Carefully review petition materials, listen to opinions, and promptly record visit information. For questions that can be answered on the spot, answer them immediately; for those that cannot be answered on the spot, inform them to wait for processing within the prescribed period. For abnormal petitions such as collective petitions, promptly report and properly handle them to prevent conflict escalation.

VI. Conduct Standards

1. Uniformly wear court uniforms according to different seasons, wear court badges as required, and wear name tags on duty. Do not open coats, unbutton, roll up sleeves, turn up trouser legs, or wear shoes that do not match the uniform; do not dye hair, paint nails, shave heads, get tattoos, or grow beards.

2. Maintain a good mental state and calm mentality at all times, with dignified and natural appearance, focused attention, civilized demeanor, and do not bring emotions to work.

3. Treat visitors with sincerity, naturalness, and kindness; use standardized language, gentle tone, and moderate pitch; do not be harsh, arrogant, or pretentious.

4. Treat every visitor equally, respect the dignity of elderly, ill, or disabled parties; provide special care for particular groups such as the elderly, weak, sick, disabled, and pregnant women.

5. When encountering visitors with intense words or emotions, remain calm and do not argue with them or ignore them; for aggressive or insulting language, express an attitude and stop it in a timely manner; for unreasonable demands or erroneous opinions, patiently explain and politely refuse.

6. For multiple visitors, strive to attend to the emotions of everyone present to prevent disorder.

7. Strictly implement post responsibilities and work procedures, work carefully, accurately, quickly, with high quality and efficiency, minimize waiting time for visitors, and avoid causing burdens to visitors due to work errors.

8. Materials to be handed to visitors shall be delivered with both hands and remind them to keep them properly; do not throw or toss materials to visitors.

9. Do not leave posts without authorization during working hours, and do not engage in activities unrelated to work. Do not consume alcohol during working hours or at noon on working days, do not smoke or eat in the workplace, and do not engage in indecent behaviors such as putting arms around shoulders, holding hands, or playing roughhouse with others.

10. Do not use any means or excuses to neglect, contradict, make things difficult for visitors, or shirk or refuse to handle relevant matters; do not argue or fight with visitors.

VII. Reception Language

1. Use civilized and standardized language during reception; do not use prohibited sentences and expressions. Do not use any abusive, sarcastic, or mocking language; do not loudly reprimand or lecture visitors.

2. Address visitors appropriately and speak properly; consider factors such as the age, gender, occupation, and education level of visitors, and try to communicate with visitors in language they can understand.

3. Language should be simple, clear, organized, and accurate.

VIII. Organizational Leadership

1. Higher and intermediate people's courts shall establish leading groups for the construction of "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows." The responsibilities of the leading groups are: to study major matters concerning the construction of "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows," coordinate and resolve difficulties and problems in the work, and supervise and inspect the progress of the work. Presidents of intermediate and basic people's courts shall personally take charge and fully implement all requirements and measures for the construction of "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows."

2. In accordance with the requirements of "politically steadfast, professionally proficient, strictly disciplined, excellent work style, and noble character," equip the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows" with staff commensurate with the tasks, strengthen the political and ideological education and trial business training of case-filing and petition judges. Implement regular job rotation; newly appointed judges and persons to be appointed as middle-level leaders shall gain experience at the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows," making the case-filing and petition posts a base for training and tempering cadres.

3. Local people's courts at all levels shall proceed from reality, adapt measures to local conditions, formulate specific work plans in accordance with the requirements of the Supreme People's Court, and ensure implementation. Strengthen publicity work on the construction of "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows," commend and publicize advanced models, summarize advanced experience, improve working mechanisms, and raise the level of case-filing and petition work.

4. Proactively accept leadership from Party committees and supervision from people's congresses, regularly or irregularly report to Party committees and people's congresses on the construction of "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows," invite deputies to people's congresses, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and law enforcement supervisors to inspect and guide work, and earnestly listen to opinions and suggestions; promptly communicate with the government, actively seek support, and promote the in-depth development of the construction of "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows."

Attachment: Referenced Civilized Expressions and Prohibited Expressions for the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows":

1. Civilized Expressions for the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows":

Hello!

Sorry to have kept you waiting!

I'm sorry!

Please wait a moment.

Please don't worry.

What difficulties do you have that we can help with?

Is there anything else you would like to add?

I'm not sure if I made myself clear.

Your documents are incomplete. Please complete them and come back.

There is an error in your form. Please fill it out again.

Is there anything else you are unclear about?

Please check the documents you are signing for.

Please sign.

Please leave your contact information, and we will get back to you soon.

2. Prohibited Expressions for the "Case-Filing and Petition Reception Windows":

Why are you here again?

I've already explained it to you!

I can't handle this matter. Go find whoever you want!

Who's in charge here, you or me?

Don't you understand?

Stop arguing (crying). If you want to argue (cry), go home and do it. You're annoying!

Are you done or not?

If you have complaints, go find the leaders. This is my attitude. What can you do about it?

What's wrong with you? You've made a mistake again!

Haven't I told you already? Why can't you understand?
